findings.issue_text: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:239–244 copies stale results from a previously read query into a new cache entry with a fresh revision when adding an uncached organization search, potentially resurrecting login lists invalidated by a concurrent IDP update.

InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:404–405 uses organization-aware enabled flags when deciding cache invalidation, so setting hideOnLogin=true while the organization is disabled skips invalidation and exposes the hidden provider from stale login cache when the organization is re-enabled.

OrganizationCacheTest.java:testCacheIDPForLogin registers both cleanup actions with the literal alias "alias" instead of the created "idp-alias-N" aliases, leaving test data behind and potentially causing cleanup failures or conflicts in subsequent tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:239–244 copies stale results from a previously read query into a new cache entry with a fresh revision when adding an uncached organization search, potentially resurrecting login lists invalidated by a concurrent IDP update.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lines 225-244 in the diff, when a cache entry exists but the current organizationId search is not cached, the code invalidates the cache key, gets a fresh revision, fetches new results for the current search, but then passes the old `query` object to the constructor: `new IdentityProviderListQuery(loaded, cacheKey, getRealm(), searchKey, cached, query)`. This constructor likely copies the existing cached searches from the old query into the new entry. If a concurrent IDP update invalidated the cache between when `query` was read and when the new entry is created, the stale results from the old query would be resurrected with a fresh revision, potentially serving outdated login IDP lists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:404–405 uses organization-aware enabled flags when deciding cache invalidation, so setting hideOnLogin=true while the organization is disabled skips invalidation and exposes the hidden provider from stale login cache when the organization is re-enabled.

adjudication.rationale: The finding references lines 404-405 which correspond to the registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate method. This method uses getLoginPredicate().test() to check if an IDP qualifies for login. Looking at the diff, getLoginPredicate() in IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java checks the IDP's own properties (like OrganizationId and BROKER_PUBLIC config), not organization-level enabled flags. The finding claims the code uses 'organization-aware enabled flags' but the actual predicate shown in the diff only checks idp.getOrganizationId() and idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC), not whether the organization itself is enabled/disabled. The scenario described (organization being disabled/re-enabled affecting cache) is not supported by the code shown in the diff.
